questions.question: If the business has a favourable bank balance, how will it appear on the Bank Statement?
options: As a credit balance, because the bank owes the business money.
As a debit balance, because it is an asset to the bank.
As a credit balance, because it is an asset to the business.
As a debit balance, because it is a liability to the business.

questions.question: What does a debit entry in the General Ledger Bank Account indicate?
options: An increase in the asset (cash received).
A decrease in the asset (cash paid).
An increase in the liability to the bank.
An overdrawn bank balance.

questions.question: Why do the Bank Account and the Bank Statement often have different balances?
options: Because of timing differences in recording transactions.
Because the bank uses different accounting principles.
Because businesses are not required to record all cash transactions.
Because the Bank Statement only shows credit transactions.

subtopics.title: Drawing the Skeleton and the Bank Balance

questions.question: Where do you post a 'favourable balance as per bank statement' on the reconciliation statement?
options: In the Credit column.
In the Debit column.
It is not posted; it is calculated at the end.
In both columns to balance.

questions.question: What is the consequence of placing a favourable bank statement balance in the debit column?
options: The entire reconciliation will be incorrect as the foundation is flawed.
The final balance will still be correct if other items are placed correctly.
The balancing figure will simply be on the opposite side.
It indicates an overdrawn account instead.

questions.question: Why is the format of the Bank Reconciliation Statement considered 'sacrosanct'?
options: Because exam marks are awarded for placing the correct number in the prescribed place.
Because the bank will reject the statement if it is not in the correct format.
Because it is required by the South African Revenue Service.
Because it makes the calculations faster.

questions.question: Where is an outstanding deposit recorded on the Bank Reconciliation Statement?
options: Credit column.
Debit column.
It is ignored until the bank processes it.
Deducted from the Bank Statement balance.

questions.question: How are outstanding cheques treated on the Bank Reconciliation Statement?
options: They are placed in the Debit column.
They are placed in the Credit column.
They are added to the outstanding deposit.
They are recorded as a liability in the ledger.

questions.question: What is the logical reason for debiting an outstanding cheque on the reconciliation statement?
options: When the bank cashes it, they will debit our account to reduce their liability to us.
It represents an increase in our assets.
It is a business expense.
Because the business has already debited the bank account.

questions.question: If the total of the Credit column is R7 420 and the Debit items total R2 130, what is the balancing figure?
options: R5 290 in the Debit column.
R5 290 in the Credit column.
R9 550 in the Debit column.
R7 420 in the Debit column.

questions.question: What does a balancing figure in the Debit column of the reconciliation statement signify?
options: A debit (favourable) balance as per the Bank Account in the General Ledger.
A credit (unfavourable) balance as per the Bank Account.
A bank overdraft.
An error in the outstanding items.

questions.question: What is the primary internal control purpose of performing regular bank reconciliations?
options: To prevent fraud and detect errors promptly.
To calculate the interest owed by the bank.
To decide whether to request a higher overdraft limit.
To prepare for the annual general meeting.
